_about: Hand-written intended-behavior descriptions (source='written') for programs with no public natural-language description, plus docstring-level rewrites of real descriptions that state exact bounds or formulas (edited_real; the original text is kept in intent_descriptions.json). Written from the ORIGINAL programs by Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code on 2026-10-23; not reviewed yet. Input to 3-build_intent_descriptions.py.

written.630-dafny_tmp_tmpz2kokaiq_Solution: Binary search over a sorted integer array. Given a value, it returns a position where that value occurs, or a special not-found result if the value does not appear in the array.
written.AssertivePrograming_tmp_tmpwf43uz0e_DivM: Arithmetic on unary natural numbers, built from zero and a successor constructor, with conversions to and from ordinary naturals, comparison, addition, subtraction and multiplication. The main method performs iterative division with remainder of one unary number by a nonzero one, returning the quotient and the remainder. Helper lemmas relate these operations to each other.
written.AssertivePrograming_tmp_tmpwf43uz0e_Find: Searches a string for the first occurrence of another string. It reports whether the second string occurs inside the first, and when it does, returns the starting position of an occurrence. Helper predicates and lemmas describe the progress of the nested search loops.
written.AssertivePrograming_tmp_tmpwf43uz0e_Merg: Recursive merge sort on an integer array. It returns a new array of the same length that is sorted and holds exactly the same elements as the input. A merge routine combines two sorted arrays into a destination array whose size is the sum of theirs, keeping the result sorted and preserving all elements.
written.CS494-final-project_tmp_tmp7nof55uq_bubb: Bubble sort for a non-empty integer array, sorting it in place into ascending order. The result contains the same elements as the original. Helper predicates describe a sorted range of the array and the position of the largest element during each pass.
written.CS5232_Project_tmp_tmpai_cfrng_LFUSimple: A least-frequently-used cache with a fixed capacity that maps integer keys to values and tracks how often each key is used. Looking up a key returns its value and updates its use count, or a special missing-key result if the key is absent, without adding or removing keys. Inserting a value may evict the least frequently used key, which a helper method finds.
written.CVS-Projto1_tmp_tmpb1o0bu8z_Hoare: Small Hoare-logic exercises. One method returns the larger of two natural numbers, another returns some value related to two ordered positive inputs, one computes Fibonacci numbers iteratively, one sums a linked list, and one finds the largest element of a non-empty array.
written.CVS-Projto1_tmp_tmpb1o0bu8z_proj1_proj1: Range sums over an integer array. A query method computes the sum of the elements between two positions, and a fast version answers the same query using a precomputed prefix-sum array. A second part converts a non-empty array into a linked list containing every element of the array.
written.CVS-handout1_tmp_tmptm52no3k_1: Range sums over an integer array. A query method computes the sum of the elements between two positions directly, and a fast version answers the same query in constant time using a precomputed prefix-sum array. A lemma splits a range sum into two adjacent parts.
written.CVS-handout1_tmp_tmptm52no3k_2: Converts an array into a linked list. The resulting list has the same length as the array, holds the array's elements in the same order, and contains no value that is not in the array.
written.Correctness_tmp_tmpwqvg5q_4_MethodCalls_: Computes Stern's diatomic sequence (the fusc function) for a non-negative input. The function is described through its recursive rules for even and odd arguments, and the method computes the value iteratively.
written.Correctness_tmp_tmpwqvg5q_4_Sorting_Tang: Given two sorted arrays of integers, determines whether some value of the first array also appears in the second, using binary search over the second array. The binary search returns the position where a value would be inserted, splitting the array into smaller and not-smaller elements.
written.Dafny-Exercises_tmp_tmpjm75muf__Session1: Given a non-empty array and a position in it, returns whether the position acts as a barrier: the elements on its left side are all smaller than the elements on its right side. It runs in linear time.
written.Dafny-Exercises_tmp_tmpjm75muf__Session2: Three ways to compute the integer square root of a non-negative number: a linear search upward, a slower search, and a binary search. All three return the same result.
written.Dafny-Exercises_tmp_tmpjm75muf__Session3: Several methods for finding the maximum of a non-empty array. Some return the position of a maximum element, including variants that return the first or the last such position, and others return the maximum value itself, which must occur in the array.
written.Dafny-Exercises_tmp_tmpjm75muf__Session4: Checks whether all elements of an array are equal. Several lemmas show equivalent formulations of the property (comparing all pairs, comparing to the first element, or comparing neighbours), and five methods implement the check in different ways.

Given two strictly increasing arrays, returns whether every element in a prefix of the first array also occurs in a prefix of the second array. The lengths of both prefixes are given as inputs, and the method runs in linear time.
written.Dafny-Exercises_tmp_tmpjm75muf__Session5: Computes the sum of the elements of an integer array. Two recursive definitions of the sum, adding from the left and from the right, are proved to agree on any slice, and two methods compute the sum with loops.
written.Dafny-Exercises_tmp_tmpjm75muf__Session6: Counts how many elements of an array of non-negative integers are even, matching a recursive counting function.
Counts how many times the minimum value occurs in a non-empty array, in a single pass, matching recursive definitions of the minimum and of the number of occurrences.
Sums the peaks of a non-empty array, where a peak is an element that is a running maximum: nothing before it is bigger. The method computes this sum in linear time, matching a recursive definition.
written.Dafny-Exercises_tmp_tmpjm75muf__Session7: Binary search on a sorted array, in iterative and recursive versions. It returns the boundary position for the searched value, that is, where the value sits or would sit in the sorted order. Further methods use it to decide whether the value occurs in the array, and to return a matching position when it does.

Two bubble sort variants that sort a segment of an integer array in place. Afterwards the segment is sorted, contains the same elements as before, and the parts of the array outside the segment are unchanged.
Selection sort on a segment of an integer array, in place. Afterwards the segment is sorted, contains the same elements as before, and the parts of the array outside the segment are unchanged.

Rearranges an integer array so that all non-negative elements come first and all negative elements come after them. It returns the position where the negative part begins, and the result is a permutation of the original array.
written.Dafny-Exercises_tmp_tmpjm75muf__Session8: Insertion sort on an integer array, in place. Afterwards the array is sorted in ascending order and contains the same elements as before.
written.Dafny-Exercises_tmp_tmpjm75muf__Session9: Given a non-empty integer array and a position in it, finds the largest sum of a contiguous segment that ends at that position. It returns the sum together with the starting point of a best segment. Two versions exist, one scanning left to right and one scanning right to left.
written.Dafny-Grind75_tmp_tmpsxfz3i4r_problems_t: The classic two-sum problem: given a sequence of integers and a target, return a pair of distinct positions whose values add up to the target. The input is assumed to contain such a pair.
written.Dafny-Practice_tmp_tmphnmt4ovh_BST: Binary search trees over integers. One method builds a search tree from a sequence without duplicates, so that the tree holds exactly the numbers of the sequence; another inserts a new number into a search tree, keeping it a search tree. A tree is a search tree when its in-order traversal is strictly ascending.
written.Dafny-demo_tmp_tmpkgr_dvdi_Dafny_BinaryS: Binary search for a key in a sorted integer array. It returns a position holding the key when the key is present, and a negative result when the key does not occur in the array.
written.Dafny-experiences_tmp_tmp150sm9qy_dafny_: Finds the position of a maximum element in a non-empty integer array.
written.DafnyExercises_tmp_tmpd6qyevja_Part1_Q1: Adds two integer arrays of the same length element by element and returns the resulting array.
written.DafnyPrograms_tmp_tmp74_f9k_c_map-multis: A multiset of integers specified abstractly and implemented with a map from elements to their counts. Adding an element always adds a copy of it; removing an element deletes one copy if present and otherwise leaves the multiset unchanged, and both report whether anything changed. Other operations return the size, compare two multisets for equality and list the elements.
written.DafnyPrograms_tmp_tmp74_f9k_c_prime-data: A database that records which natural numbers are prime. Numbers can be inserted either as known primes or after testing their primality, and a lookup answers Yes, No or Unknown depending on whether the number is stored and whether it is prime, without changing the database. A helper tests primality directly.
written.DafnyProjects_tmp_tmp2acw_s4s_findMax: Finds the maximum value in a non-empty array of real numbers.
written.Dafny_Learning_Experience_tmp_tmpuxvcet_: Counts the even numbers in a prefix of a sequence, both directly and using a precomputed array of running counts. Other methods fill in that precomputed array, build a two-dimensional table from an array, and multiply two non-negative integers by repeated addition.

Linear search variants. The generic search returns the first position whose element satisfies a predicate, or a not-found result when none does. Other variants search a prefix of an array, or look for a given element and report its position in a one-based style, or not found.

Two stacks sharing a single fixed-capacity array, one growing from each end. Each stack supports push, which reports failure when the shared space is full, pop and peek, which report failure when that stack is empty, and emptiness and fullness checks. A validity predicate ties the abstract stacks to the shared array.
Searches the first part of an array for a given natural number. It returns a one-based position where the element was found, or a not-found result, together with the number of elements examined.

A checksum calculator that keeps a string and a running checksum of it, defined as the sum of the character codes reduced modulo a fixed prime. Appending text updates the stored string and its checksum; the data and the checksum can be read back.
written.Dafny_Programs_tmp_tmp99966ew4_binary_se: Binary search for a value in a sorted integer array. It returns a position holding the value when present, and a negative result when the value does not occur.
written.Dafny_Programs_tmp_tmp99966ew4_lemma: Finds a zero in an array of non-negative integers whose values never drop sharply from one position to the next. Because of this, the search can skip ahead by the current value, and a lemma justifies the skip. It returns the position of a zero, or a negative result if there is none.
written.Dafny_Verify_tmp_tmphq7j0row_AI_agent_va: Small verification examples: computing a power of two iteratively, finding the maximum of an array of naturals (with a default when the array is empty), cubing a number, incrementing every entry of a matrix, copying one matrix into another of the same shape, doubling every element of an array into another array, and rotating an array left or right by one position.
written.Dafny_Verify_tmp_tmphq7j0row_AI_agent_ve: Computes a power of two iteratively for a non-negative exponent, matching a recursive definition.
Copies every entry of a source matrix into a destination matrix of the same shape.
Writes twice each element of a source array into a destination array of the same length.
Rotates a non-empty array to the right by one position in place, so the last element moves to the front and every other element shifts one place towards the end.
written.Dafny_Verify_tmp_tmphq7j0row_Fine_Tune_E: A loop benchmark: starting from two equal non-negative inputs, it counts both down together until they reach the counter, and returns the final values. The goal is to show that the two values stay in step.

A loop benchmark: it walks through the numbers up to a positive limit and, at arbitrary steps, remembers the current number. The goal is to show that the remembered number is always a valid index below the limit.

A loop benchmark: it counts up to a non-negative limit, increasing one counter at every step and a second counter at every other step. The goal is to show the relationship between the two counters when the step count is even.

A loop benchmark: it counts up to a non-negative limit while accumulating a running total of the counter. The goal is to show a lower bound on the final values in terms of the limit and an extra parameter.
Binary search on a sorted integer array that returns the insertion point of a key, the position where the key belongs in the sorted order.
Computes the sum of all elements of a non-empty integer array, matching a recursive definition of the sum of a prefix.
Finds the maximum of the first part of an integer array, whose length is given.
written.Dafny_Verify_tmp_tmphq7j0row_Generated_C: A loop benchmark: it decreases a starting value once for each step up to a limit and returns it. The goal is to show a bound on the result.
Counts how many times a value occurs in the first part of an integer array, matching a recursive counting function.
Finds the minimum value of a non-empty integer array.
Multiplies two non-negative integers using repeated addition.
Starting from the product of two non-negative numbers, repeatedly subtracts one of them while counting the other down, and returns what is left, which should end at zero.
written.Dafny_Verify_tmp_tmphq7j0row_Test_Cases_: Basic loop exercises over a non-negative bound: counting up to the bound with two different loop conditions, counting down to zero with two different loop conditions, and computing a quotient by repeated subtraction.
written.Dafny_Verify_tmp_tmphq7j0row_dataset_C_c: A loop benchmark translated from C: for a given non-negative number of steps, it increases two counters by small amounts, choosing arbitrarily at each step which counter gets the larger increase. The goal is to show how the counters' total relates to the number of steps.
A loop benchmark translated from C: for a positive input, it repeatedly adds a fixed step to an accumulator once per count up to the input, and returns the accumulator.
A loop benchmark translated from C: it decreases a starting value once for each step up to a limit and returns it. The goal is to show a bound on the result.
written.Dafny_Verify_tmp_tmphq7j0row_dataset_bql: Finds the minimum among the first elements of an integer array, where the number of elements to consider is given.
Adds up the first elements of an integer array whose elements are bounded by a given maximum. The goal is to show that the total is bounded accordingly.
Computes the square of a non-negative integer using repeated addition.
written.Dafny_Verify_tmp_tmphq7j0row_dataset_err: Decides whether a non-negative integer is even, matching a recursive definition that alternates between even and odd.
written.Dafny_tmp_tmp0wu8wmfr_Heimaverkefni 1_Li: Searches a segment of a sequence for a value, once recursively and once with a loop. Each version returns the last position in the segment holding the value, or a not-found result if the value does not occur in the segment.
written.Dafny_tmp_tmp0wu8wmfr_Heimaverkefni 2_Bi: Binary search, recursive and iterative, over a segment of a sequence of reals sorted in descending order. It returns the position where the searched value belongs in that order.
written.Dafny_tmp_tmp0wu8wmfr_Heimaverkefni 3_In: Insertion sort that turns a multiset of integers into a sorted sequence with exactly the same elements. A binary search helper finds where a value belongs in a sorted sequence.
written.Dafny_tmp_tmp0wu8wmfr_Heimaverkefni 3_Se: Selection sort that turns a multiset of integers into a sorted sequence with exactly the same elements. A helper returns the smallest value of a non-empty multiset.
written.Dafny_tmp_tmp0wu8wmfr_Heimaverkefni 8_H8: Quickselect on multisets. Partition picks a pivot from a non-empty multiset and splits the remaining elements into those on either side of the pivot. QuickSelect uses it to find the element of a given rank, returning it along with the elements that come before and after it in sorted order.
written.Dafny_tmp_tmp0wu8wmfr_tests_Search1000: Bentley's fixed-size binary search from Programming Pearls, applied to the sorted beginning of a large array. It returns the position where the searched value belongs. Further versions, iterative and recursive, handle sorted segments whose size has a special power-of-two form.
written.Dafny_tmp_tmp0wu8wmfr_tests_SumIntsLoop: Computes the sum of the positive integers up to a non-negative bound with a loop. The result matches a recursive definition and the usual closed-form formula.
written.Dafny_tmp_tmpmvs2dmry_examples2: Arithmetic exercises on naturals: addition by repeated increments, multiplication by repeated addition, the greatest common divisor of two positive numbers by repeated subtraction, and raising a non-negative real to a natural power by repeated squaring.
written.Dafny_tmp_tmpmvs2dmry_pancakesort_findma: Part of pancake sort: returns the position of a largest element within the first part of a non-empty array, whose length is given. The array's contents are not changed.
written.Dafny_tmp_tmpmvs2dmry_pancakesort_flip: Part of pancake sort: reverses the beginning of a non-empty array up to a given position, in place, leaving the rest of the array unchanged.
written.Dafny_tmp_tmpv_d3qi10_2_min: Returns the smaller of two integers, both as a function and as a method, and finds a minimum element of a non-empty integer array.
written.Dafny_tmp_tmpv_d3qi10_3_cumsum: Computes the cumulative (prefix) sums of a non-empty integer array into a second, distinct array of the same length, so that each entry of the second array holds the sum of the input up to that position.
written.FMSE-2022-2023_tmp_tmp6_x_ba46_Lab10_Lab: A bounded list that may only contain odd integers. It supports inserting at a position or at either end while capacity remains, removing an element or the element at a position, popping from either end, reading the length and the element at a position, binary search on a sorted list, and merging two sorted lists. Every operation keeps the capacity fixed and the list valid.
written.Final-Project-Dafny_tmp_tmpmcywuqox_Atte: Increments every element of a non-empty integer array by one, in place.
Finds the maximum of a non-empty array of non-negative integers and returns both its value and a position where it occurs.
Binary search for a value in a non-empty sorted integer array. It returns a position holding the value, or a position outside the array if the value is not present.
Sorts an integer array in place into ascending order. A helper finds the position of the smallest element in the remaining part of the array, starting from a given position.
Insertion sort on an integer array, sorting it in place into ascending order.

Quicksort on integer sequences. A threshold helper splits a sequence into the elements on either side of a pivot value, keeping every element exactly once. The sort returns a sequence with the same elements as its input.
written.FlexWeek_tmp_tmpc_tfdj_3_reverse: Iteratively builds a new character array holding the elements of a non-empty input array in reverse order. The input array is not modified.
written.Formal-Verification-Project_tmp_tmp9gmws: String utilities with matching specification predicates: checking whether one string is a prefix of another, whether one string occurs as a substring of another, whether two strings share a common substring of a given length, and finding the length of the longest common substring. Lemmas show that each property and its negated form are complementary.
written.Formal-Verification_tmp_tmpuyt21wjt_Dafn: String utilities with matching specification predicates: checking whether one string is a prefix of another, whether one string occurs as a substring of another, whether two strings share a common substring of a given length, and finding the length of the longest common substring. Lemmas show that each property and its negated form are complementary.
written.Formal-methods-of-software-development_t: Introductory exercises: methods that return a pair of values built from an input and a positive offset, computing factorials iteratively in two ways, and computing the square of a positive number by summing consecutive odd numbers, with a lemma relating that sum to the square.
written.Formal_Verification_With_Dafny_tmp_tmp5j: A stack of integers with limited capacity, stored in an array. It supports initialisation with a positive capacity, an emptiness check, peeking at and popping the top element of a non-empty stack, pushing onto a stack that is not full, shifting all elements down by one, and a second push that discards the oldest element when the stack is full.
written.HATRA-2022-Paper_tmp_tmp5texxy8l_copilot: Binary search on a sorted array of distinct integers. It returns the position of the target when present, and a not-found result otherwise.

Finds the largest sum of any contiguous subarray of a non-empty integer array (Kadane's algorithm). A predicate states that the result is the maximum over all subarray sums, and a recursive function sums a range of the array.

Sorts an integer array of moderate size, returning an array sorted in ascending order with the same elements as the input. Helper predicates describe a sorted range and a pivot position used during sorting.
The two-sum problem on an array: given an array that contains two entries adding up to a target, return two different positions whose values add up to the target.
written.M2_tmp_tmp2laaavvl_Software Verification: Counts up from zero with a loop until reaching a non-negative input, and returns the final count, which equals the input.
written.MFES_2021_tmp_tmpuljn8zd9_FCUL_Exercises: Linear search for a key in a non-empty integer array. It returns a position holding the key, or the array length when the key is not found.
written.MFES_2021_tmp_tmpuljn8zd9_PracticalClass: Sorts an integer array in place using insertion sort. Afterwards the array is in ascending order and holds the same elements as before.
written.MIEIC_mfes_tmp_tmpq3ho7nve_TP3_binary_se: Finds a value in a sorted integer array with binary search and returns its position, or a not-found result if the value is absent.
written.MIEIC_mfes_tmp_tmpq3ho7nve_exams_mt2_19_: Partitions a non-empty array around a chosen pivot by reordering its elements, placing them on either side of the pivot according to how they compare with it. It returns the pivot's final position, and the array keeps the same elements.
written.MIEIC_mfes_tmp_tmpq3ho7nve_exams_special: Uses binary search to find where a value can be inserted into a sorted array so that it stays sorted. The array itself is not changed.
written.Program-Verification-Dataset_tmp_tmpgbdr: Higher-order array exercises: filling an array so that each entry is a given function applied to its position, and a sorting routine that orders an array according to a supplied comparison function.

Finds a maximum element of a non-empty array of any type, using a supplied comparison that is total and transitive. The result is an element of the array that compares as at least as large as every element.
Insertion sort on an integer array, sorting it in place into ascending order.

Multiplies two integer matrices whose inner dimensions agree. The result has as many rows as the first matrix and as many columns as the second, and each entry is the product of the corresponding row and column.

Models the hundred prisoners and a light bulb puzzle. The counting strategy is run for a set of prisoners with one designated counter until the counter can announce that everyone has visited the room. A lemma states that a proper subset is smaller than its superset.
Returns a new character array holding the elements of a non-empty input array in reverse order.

Sorting algorithms from Program Proofs: selection sort and quicksort on integer arrays, both sorting in place while preserving the elements. Quicksort works on a range of the array, using a partition step around a pivot, and only swaps elements within that range.
Multiplies an integer by a non-negative integer using repeated addition. A helper function turns a string into the set of its characters.

LeetCode's find pivot index: given a non-empty sequence of integers, return a position where the sum of the elements to its left equals the sum of the elements to its right, or a not-found result if no such position exists. Lemmas show that two recursive definitions of the sum agree.

Bubble sort for a non-empty integer array, sorting it in place into ascending order while keeping the same elements. Helper predicates describe a sorted range and the position of the largest element during each pass.
Bubble sort for a non-empty integer array, sorting it in place into ascending order while keeping the same elements.
Adds a non-negative integer to another integer by incrementing one at a time. A second version spells out by hand the verification conditions of the loop.
Returns the position of a maximum element in a non-empty integer array.

Two loop exercises: counting up to a natural number, matching a recursive definition, and computing the total of a sequence of naturals, matching a recursive sum, with a lemma that extends a prefix sum by one element.

A simple binary decision diagram. Each node represents a boolean function over a fixed number of input bits, and evaluating the diagram on an input of the right length returns the value of the represented function.

A singly linked list whose nodes track the abstract sequence they represent. It supports creating a one-element list, prepending an element, skipping the head, and reversing the list in place so that it holds the original elements in reverse order.

A verification competition problem: given an array whose values all lie in a small range determined by its length and which is known to contain two different values that each occur at least twice, find two such duplicated values. The method makes one pass, recording what it has seen in a temporary array.

Two classic verified programs: Turing's additive factorial, which computes a factorial using only additions, and Hoare's FIND, which rearranges an array so that the element at a chosen position ends up in its sorted place, with smaller elements on one side and larger ones on the other.

The Boyer and Moore majority vote algorithm. Given a sequence of votes in which one candidate has a strict majority, it finds that candidate; a second version does not assume a majority exists and reports either the winner or that there is none. Lemmas relate counts over adjacent ranges and over two different candidates.

A container that stores a set of things and retrieves one matching a given criterion, refined in steps from an abstract specification to an array-based implementation. Storing adds the thing to the contents; retrieving, when some stored thing matches, returns a matching stored thing without changing the contents.

A growable list class with an iterator. Adding an element appends it to the list's contents, an iterator yields the elements in order, and a client collects elements from the iterator until it sees a stop value.

Euclid's proof that there are infinitely many primes. For any number there is a larger prime, and no finite set contains every prime; the proof builds a new prime from the product of a set of primes. Supporting lemmas cover products of sets, an alternative definition of primality, and factoring composite numbers.

A model of crash-consistent memory updates using an undo log. Ghost state tracks the memory, the log, the number of logged entries and a countdown until a simulated crash; steps write to memory or to the log and may crash. Transactions begin, record old values in the log, and on recovery the memory returns to its state before the transaction.

Fast exponentiation of naturals by repeated squaring, using the binary representation of the exponent. Helper functions convert numbers to and from bit sequences, and lemmas relate exponents of sums to products and describe how appending bits changes the value.
Linear search for a key in an integer array. It returns a position holding the key, or a negative result when the key does not occur.

Termination examples from Katz and Manna: McCarthy's well-known nested recursive function computed with a loop, a greatest common divisor computation on positive numbers, and a determinant computation on a square matrix.

Computes sums of cubes of consecutive integers over a range, and from zero up to a bound. Lemmas relate sums over ranges, show that the sum of the first cubes equals the square of the corresponding triangular number, and give the closed form of that triangular number.

A deceptively simple sorting algorithm that runs two nested loops over all pairs of positions and swaps the two elements whenever the first position comes before the second and the order calls for it. It sorts an integer array in place into ascending order, and since it only swaps, the result is a permutation of the input.
written.Programmverifikation-und-synthese_tmp_tm: Two exercises: summing the first odd numbers for a positive count, which yields a perfect square, and integer division with remainder of a non-negative number by a positive divisor, in a specified and an implemented version.

Iterative versions of three recursive functions: Fibonacci numbers for a positive index, factorials of naturals, and the greatest common divisor of two positive integers computed by repeated subtraction.
Computes the greatest common divisor of two positive integers iteratively by repeated subtraction, matching a recursive definition. A second recursive definition uses a different termination measure.

Computes the greatest common divisor of two positive integers iteratively by repeated subtraction, matching a recursive definition. A second recursive definition uses the larger argument as its termination measure.
Building blocks for selection sort on an integer array: swapping two elements, finding the position of the smallest element from a given starting position onward, and the sort itself.

Exercises on weakest preconditions: two ways of squaring a natural number with loops, a method that returns a number whose square lies between two inputs that are far enough apart, and examples showing how an unsatisfiable specification makes absurd conclusions provable.
Introductory loops: summing the numbers from one up to a non-negative bound, which proves Gauss's formula, and summing the first odd numbers, which yields a perfect square.
written.ProjectosCVS_tmp_tmp_02_gmcw_Handout 1_C: Two arithmetic exercises: peasant multiplication of an integer by a positive integer using halving and doubling, with a supporting lemma, and Euclidean division of a non-negative number by a positive number, returning quotient and remainder.
written.QS_BoilerPlate1_tmp_tmpa29vtz9__Ex2: Merge sort on an integer array. A helper copies a non-empty range of an array into a new array, another merges two adjacent sorted ranges into one sorted range without touching the rest of the array, and the sort applies these recursively to sort the whole array.
written.SENG2011_tmp_tmpgk5jq85q_ass1_ex8: Modifies an array of natural numbers in place so that every element becomes even.
written.SENG2011_tmp_tmpgk5jq85q_ass2_ex3: Sorts a string made only of the letters b, a and d into the order all b's, then all a's, then all d's, in the style of the Dutch national flag problem. The result has the same letters as the input.
written.SENG2011_tmp_tmpgk5jq85q_exam_ex2: Returns the position of the first occurrence of the minimum value in a non-empty integer array.
written.SENG2011_tmp_tmpgk5jq85q_flex_ex1: Returns the sum of all elements of a non-empty integer array, matching a recursive prefix-sum function.
written.SENG2011_tmp_tmpgk5jq85q_flex_ex2: Returns the maximum of a non-empty array of naturals.
written.SENG2011_tmp_tmpgk5jq85q_p1: Returns a new character array holding the elements of a non-empty input array in reverse order.
written.Software-Verification_tmp_tmpv4ueky2d_Be: LeetCode's best time to buy and sell stock: given a non-empty array of bounded non-negative daily prices, return the largest profit from buying on one day and selling on a later day.
written.Software-Verification_tmp_tmpv4ueky2d_Co: LeetCode's contains duplicate, for a non-empty sequence of bounded integers. The method's boolean result reports whether the elements are pairwise distinct.

LeetCode's counting bits: for a non-negative bounded input, return an array giving, for every number from zero up to the input, how many one bits it has in binary. Each entry is computed from the entry for the number with its last bit removed.
written.Software-Verification_tmp_tmpv4ueky2d_Lo: LeetCode's longest increasing subsequence: given a non-empty array of bounded integers, compute the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence using dynamic programming. A helper returns the larger of two integers.
written.Software-Verification_tmp_tmpv4ueky2d_No: LeetCode's non-overlapping intervals: given a non-empty list of intervals with bounded endpoints, count how many intervals must be removed so that the rest do not overlap. The intervals are first sorted by end point with a bubble sort.
written.Software-Verification_tmp_tmpv4ueky2d_Re: LeetCode's remove duplicates from sorted array: given a non-empty sorted sequence of bounded integers, return a strictly increasing sequence containing exactly the same values.

LeetCode's remove element: removes all occurrences of a value from a small array of bounded non-negative integers in place, moving the kept elements to the front, and returns how many elements remain.
written.Software-Verification_tmp_tmpv4ueky2d_Va: LeetCode's valid anagram: given two strings of equal length, decide whether one is a rearrangement of the other by comparing their letter multisets. A helper checks whether two multisets of characters are equal.
Checks whether a non-empty character array reads the same forwards and backwards.
written.Software-building-and-verification-Proje: Loop exercises: computing Fibonacci numbers iteratively, summing a linked list of integers, finding the maximum of a non-empty array scanning forwards and backwards, and summing the naturals up to a bound by counting down.

A bounded set of integers stored in an array, with an abstract view of its contents that hides the representation, and a variant that only stores positive integers. It can report its size and capacity, test membership, add a new element while space remains, and find the position of an element.

Range sums over an integer array: a query computes the sum of a range directly, and a fast query answers it from a prefix-sum array, with a lemma splitting a range sum in two. A second part converts an array into a linked list holding exactly the array's elements.
written.TFG_tmp_tmpbvsao41w_Algoritmos Dafny_div: Iterative integer division: for a non-negative dividend and a positive divisor, computes the quotient and the remainder by repeated subtraction.
written.TFG_tmp_tmpbvsao41w_Algoritmos Dafny_sum: Iteratively computes the sum of all components of an integer array, matching a recursive function that sums the array from a given position to the end.
written.VerifiedMergeSortDafny_tmp_tmpva7qms1b_M: Merging for merge sort: two sorted sequences are merged into a range of an array so that the range becomes sorted and contains exactly the elements of both sequences. Predicates describe sorted sequences, sorted array ranges and the merged property.
written.Workshop_tmp_tmp0cu11bdq_Lecture_Answers: Finds the maximum of an integer array.
Selection sort on an integer array, sorting it in place into ascending order.
Computes the sum of all elements of an integer array, matching a recursive function that sums a prefix.
Computes the triangular number of a non-negative integer, the sum of all positive integers up to it, with a loop.
written.Workshop_tmp_tmp0cu11bdq_Workshop_Answer: Reverses an integer array in place.
Creates an array of a given non-negative length filled with non-negative values in ascending order.
written.assertive-programming-assignment-1_tmp_t: Given a sorted sequence and a key, returns the range of positions holding the key, which is empty when the key is absent. It uses a generic binary search parameterised by a comparison function.

Given a sorted sequence that contains two elements adding up to a target, returns two positions, the first before the second, whose values add up to the target. It moves a low index up and a high index down depending on whether the current sum is too small or too large.
written.bbfny_tmp_tmpw4m0jvl0_enjoying: Tutorial exercises: returning one value above and one below an input, the larger of two integers, absolute value, Fibonacci numbers, linear search returning a position of a key or a negative result, and finding the position of a maximum in a non-empty array, with sortedness predicates.
written.circular-queue-implemetation_tmp_tmpnulf: A queue of integers stored in a circular array that grows as needed. Inserting adds an item, with helper methods for the different layouts of the front and rear markers (empty queue, insertion at the end, insertion into a gap); removing returns the item at the front and advances the front marker around the circle. The abstract content of the queue is tracked as a sequence.
written.cmsc433_tmp_tmpe3ob3a0o_dafny_project1_p: A set of small specification exercises: adding one to a non-negative number, swapping two array elements, integer division with remainder by a positive divisor, adding two arrays element by element, Euclid's greatest common divisor, checking whether an array is sorted, checking primality, reversing an array into a fresh array, and checking whether a sorted array has duplicates.
written.cs245-verification_tmp_tmp0h_nxhqp_A8_Q1: Raises an integer to a non-negative power with a loop that multiplies an accumulator once per step, matching a recursive power function.
written.cs245-verification_tmp_tmp0h_nxhqp_Sorti: An example showing a weak sorting specification: the method is meant to sort an integer array whose length is given, but its postcondition only asks for the result to be ordered, so code that overwrites the array with increasing values also satisfies it.
written.cs245-verification_tmp_tmp0h_nxhqp_power: Raises a non-negative integer to a non-negative power with a loop, matching a recursive power function, with intermediate assertions that spell out the Hoare-logic proof.
written.cs245-verification_tmp_tmp0h_nxhqp_quick: The partition step of quicksort: rearranges the first part of an integer array around a pivot value, so that elements on each side of the pivot are grouped together, and returns the boundary. The array remains a permutation of the original.
written.dafl_tmp_tmp_r3_8w3y_dafny_examples_uiow: Binary search on a sorted integer array that returns whether a given key occurs in it. Two equivalent definitions of sortedness are given, comparing all pairs or only neighbours.
Linear search for a key in an integer array. It returns the first position where the key appears, or a negative result if the array does not contain the key.

Examples of working with arrays: setting the end points of a non-empty array, aliasing between arrays, creating a fresh array of a fixed size, initialising every entry to a default value, updating particular entries relative to their old values, incrementing every element, and copying one array into another of the same length.
written.dafleet_tmp_tmpa2e4kb9v_0001-0050_0001-t: LeetCode's two sum: given a sequence of integers for which some solution exists, return two different positions whose values add up to the target. It uses a map from values to positions to find each element's partner in one pass.
written.dafleet_tmp_tmpa2e4kb9v_0001-0050_0005-l: LeetCode's longest palindromic substring. It returns a longest palindromic substring of the input together with its start and end positions. One version expands around every center; a second implements Manacher's linear-time algorithm.
written.dafny-duck_tmp_tmplawbgxjo_ex3: Sorts a string made only of the letters b, a and d so that all b's come first and all d's come last, in the style of the Dutch national flag problem. The result has the same letters as the input.
written.dafny-duck_tmp_tmplawbgxjo_p3: Returns the maximum value in a non-empty array of natural numbers.
written.dafny-duck_tmp_tmplawbgxjo_p4: Given two non-empty integer arrays, returns a single array containing the elements of the first followed by the elements of the second.
written.dafny-exercise_tmp_tmpouftptir_countNeg: Counts the negative elements of an integer array, matching a recursive counting function.
written.dafny-exercise_tmp_tmpouftptir_maxArray: Returns the maximum value in a non-empty integer array.
written.dafny-exercise_tmp_tmpouftptir_prac1_ex2: Deletes the character at a given position of a non-empty character array in place: the characters before it stay the same, the characters after it shift one place towards the front, and the freed last slot is filled with a period.
written.dafny-exercise_tmp_tmpouftptir_reverse: Returns a new character array holding the elements of a non-empty input array in reverse order, without modifying the input.
written.dafny-exercises_tmp_tmp5mvrowrx_paper_kr: The linked-list example from Leino's paper on specifying object-oriented software. Each node tracks the abstract list it represents and its footprint; methods create a one-element list, skip the head, prepend an element, and reverse the list in place.
written.dafny-language-server_tmp_tmpkir0kenl_Te: VSComp 2010 problem one: computes the sum and the maximum of an array of non-negative integers with a given length, and proves that the sum is bounded by the length times the maximum.
Binary search for a key in a sorted integer array. It returns a position holding the key, or a not-found result when the key is absent.
Copies a sequence into an array starting at a given position, where the sequence fits within the array. Afterwards the array holds the sequence at that position and is unchanged elsewhere.

Compilation tests for arrays. Linear search returns the position of the first occurrence of a key, or the array length if it is absent; other methods print arrays, test initialisation, and build a diagonal matrix of given dimensions.
Reverses a linked list in place within a closed region of nodes, so that the result is null or a node of the same region and the region stays closed under the next pointers.
In-place matrix operations: mirroring each row of a matrix left to right, and transposing a square matrix.
COST verification competition 2011, problem one: returns the position of a maximum element of a non-empty integer array, using the classic two-pointer elimination algorithm.

Rounding against a sorted array of thresholds, as used in an interval abstract domain. Rounding down finds the nearest threshold below a value and rounding up finds the nearest threshold above it, each with a special result when there is no such threshold.
Finds a maximum-sum segment of an integer sequence and returns its start and end.

Computes the factorial of a positive whole number using only addition. An outer loop steps through the numbers up to the input, and an inner loop builds each next factorial by repeatedly adding the previous one. The result equals the mathematical factorial of the input.

A compilation test for higher-order functions. A reference cell class stores a value given at construction, and the main method builds and applies lambdas, including closures over local variables and over a mutable cell, and a function built up in a loop.
Returns the largest element of a non-empty sequence of integers. A lemma shows that the maximum is uniquely determined by its defining properties.

The VACID composite pattern: nodes in a tree each hold a value and the sum of the values in their subtree. Updating a node's value, attaching a child tree and detaching a subtree each keep all sums consistent while leaving unrelated nodes unchanged.

VSTTE 2012 two-way sort: sorts an array of booleans in place so that all false values come before all true values, using swaps, and the result is a permutation of the original. A swap helper exchanges two distinct positions and leaves the rest unchanged.
written.dafny-programs_tmp_tmpcwodh6qh_src_expt: Raises an integer to a natural power with a loop, matching a recursive definition. A lemma shows that multiplying two powers of the same base adds the exponents.
written.dafny-rope_tmp_tmpl4v_njmy_Rope: A rope data structure for strings: a binary tree whose leaves hold non-empty pieces of text and whose inner nodes store weights. It supports reporting a substring, converting to a string, reading the character at a position, concatenating two ropes, splitting a rope at a position, inserting one rope into another, and deleting a range.
written.dafny-workout_tmp_tmp0abkw6f8_starter_ex: Returns the position of a maximum element in a non-empty integer array.
written.dafny_examples_tmp_tmp8qotd4ez_leetcode_: LeetCode's sqrt: returns the integer square root of a non-negative integer. A lemma shows that the integer square root is unique.

LeetCode's find the celebrity: among a small group of people, a celebrity is someone everyone else knows who knows no one else. The method returns the celebrity if there is one, or a not-found result otherwise, eliminating candidates in one pass and then checking the remaining one.
written.dafny_examples_tmp_tmp8qotd4ez_test_shuf: Shuffles an array: returns a new array of the same length containing the same elements in random order, using a random-number helper that returns a value in a range and a swap helper. Lemmas relate multisets, sets and membership in sequences.
written.dafny_projects_tmp_tmpjutqwjv4_tutorial_: Exercises from the Dafny online tutorial: Fibonacci numbers, linear search and binary search returning a position or a negative not-found result, updating a sequence, finding a zero in an array whose values never drop sharply using a skipping lemma, counting true values in a boolean sequence, and paths in a closed graph.
written.dafny_tmp_tmp59p638nn_examples_GenericSe: Generic selection sort over any element type with a supplied less-than comparison. Sorting leaves the array ordered and holding the same elements, and a measurable comparison operation counts how many comparisons are made, which stays within a quadratic bound in the array length.
written.dafny_tmp_tmp59p638nn_examples_Selection: Selection sort on an integer array, in two versions, sorting it in place into ascending order. Helper predicates state that a range is ordered and that the array's elements are preserved.
written.dafny_tmp_tmp59p638nn_examples_minmax2: Returns the difference between the largest and the smallest element of a non-empty integer array, using recursive definitions of the minimum and maximum of a sequence.
written.dafny_tmp_tmp59p638nn_examples_realExpon: Axiomatised real powers and logarithms with a positive base. Lemmas state that power and logarithm undo each other, that the logarithm of a product is a sum of logarithms, and how the power grows when the exponent increases by one. A method computes the power for a positive natural exponent by repeated multiplication.
written.feup-mfes_tmp_tmp6_a1y5a5_examples_Selec: Selection sort on an array of reals, sorting it in place into ascending order and keeping the same elements. A helper finds the position of a minimum value in a non-empty range of the array.
written.formal-methods-in-software-engineering_t: Lab exercises on Hoare logic: a Hoare triple about updating a running square, loop rules with assumptions and invariants, the sum of the squares of the naturals up to a bound with a lemma giving its closed form, and integer division with remainder of a non-negative number by a positive one.
written.formal-verification_tmp_tmpoepcssay_stri: String utilities with matching specification predicates: checking whether one string is a prefix of another, whether one string occurs as a substring of another, whether two strings share a common substring of a given length, and finding the length of the longest common substring. Lemmas show that each property and its negated form are complementary.
written.formal_verication_dafny_tmp_tmpwgl2qz28_: The Bulls and Cows game: given a secret and a guess of the same short length, each made of distinct natural numbers, count the bulls (right number in the right place) and the cows (right number in the wrong place). Recursive functions define both counts.

Sorts a non-empty sequence of DNA bases into the order A, C, G, T, adapting the Dutch national flag algorithm to four values. A helper swaps two positions of a sequence, and the result has the same bases as the input.
written.fv2020-tms_tmp_tmpnp85b47l_modeling_conc: Models a ticket-based mutual exclusion protocol in which processes cycle through thinking, hungry and eating. A process takes a ticket when it becomes hungry, may eat when its ticket is being served, and advances the serving number when it leaves. A lemma proves that no two processes eat at the same time, and run methods schedule processes repeatedly.
written.ironsync-osdi2023_tmp_tmpx80antoe_linear: C++ compilation tests for arrays of unsigned integers: returning a null or a small fresh array, linear search that returns the first position of a key or the length when it is absent, and printing arrays.
written.laboratory_tmp_tmps8ws6mu2_dafny-tutoria: Returns the position of a maximum element in a non-empty integer array.
written.llm-verified-eval_tmp_tmpd2deqn_i_dafny_: A HumanEval problem: given a string, if it contains any letters, flip the case of every letter and leave other characters alone; if it contains no letters, return the string reversed. Helper functions identify letters, toggle case, and reverse a sequence.

A HumanEval problem: given a non-empty sequence of integers, return the sequence of rolling maxima, where each entry is the largest value seen up to that position. A helper finds the maximum of a non-empty sequence.
written.metodosFormais_tmp_tmp4q2kmya4_T1-Metodo: Computes the sum of all elements of an array of naturals, matching a recursive function that sums a prefix.
written.pucrs-metodos-formais-t1_tmp_tmp7gvq3cw4: A queue of integers stored in an array that starts with a small default capacity and grows when full. It supports reporting its size and whether it is empty, adding to the back, removing from the front of a non-empty queue, testing membership, and concatenating two queues.
written.se2011_tmp_tmp71eb82zt_ass1_ex4: Computes the square of a non-negative integer.
written.software_analysis_tmp_tmpmt6bo9sf_ss: Selection sort on an integer array, sorting it in place into ascending order so that the result is a permutation of the original. A helper returns the position of a minimum element within a non-empty range of the array.
written.specTesting_tmp_tmpueam35lx_examples_bin: Specification testing for binary search on a sorted sequence. The original specification returns a position holding the key or a negative result when it is absent; a deterministic version also fixes the not-found result and requires the first matching position; deliberately wrong variants and transition predicates are used to test whether specifications are strong enough.
written.summer-school-2020_tmp_tmpn8nf7zf0_chapt: Tests whether a natural number greater than one is prime by checking its possible divisors with a loop, matching a predicate defining primality.
Merge sort on integer sequences. Merging two sorted sequences produces a sorted sequence with the elements of both, and the sort returns a sorted sequence with the same elements as its input.
written.t1_MF_tmp_tmpi_sqie4j_exemplos_colecoes_: Computes the sum of all elements of an array of naturals, matching a recursive function that sums a prefix.

Deletes a run of characters from a line of text stored in a character array: the characters before the deleted part stay the same and the characters after it shift left to close the gap. The line's length and the deleted range must fit within the array.
written.tangent-finder_tmp_tmpgyzf44ve_circles: Given an array of circle radii and a sorted array of positions on a line, all non-negative, decides whether some radius equals some position, which corresponds to a circle being tangent to a line.
written.test-generation-examples_tmp_tmptwyqofrp: A set of integers stored as a sequence without duplicates. It can be created empty or from a duplicate-free sequence, report its size, add or remove an element (leaving the set unchanged when the element is already present or absent), test membership, and compute intersections and unions.
written.veri-sparse_tmp_tmp15fywna6_dafny_concur: A proof of concept for concurrent matrix-vector multiplication: each process is assigned one row of the matrix and accumulates that row's product with the vector one column at a time. written.veri-sparse_tmp_tmp15fywna6_dafny_dspmsp: Multiplies a sparse matrix in compressed form by a sparse vector, producing a dense result vector of the matrix's row count. written.veri-sparse_tmp_tmp15fywna6_dafny_spmv: Multiplies a sparse matrix in compressed sparse row form by a dense vector. The result has one entry per row, and each entry is the sum of the row's stored values times the matching vector entries.
written.verified-using-dafny_tmp_tmp7jatpjyn_lon: Finds the longest run of consecutive zeros in a non-empty integer array, returning its length and starting position. Every longer stretch of the array contains a non-zero element.
written.vfag_tmp_tmpc29dxm1j_sumar_componentes: Computes the sum of all components of an integer array, matching a recursive function that sums the array from a given position to the end.
